what: Ameriprise Financial is a wealth management firm. About 10,000 financial advisers manage money for American households, and it also runs the Columbia Threadneedle asset manager and sells insurance and annuities.
customers: Mass-affluent and high-net-worth American households, plus institutional investors in its funds.
money: fees on client assets managed by its advisers
moat: Adviser relationships with clients who rarely move, and the scale to offer advisers technology and products that keep them from joining a rival.
risks: Fee revenue falls when markets fall
Asset management has seen persistent outflows industry-wide
Interest earned on client cash drops when rates fall
Annuity liabilities are long-dated and rate-sensitive
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 57% with a 26% operating margin
Client assets have grown steadily through adviser recruitment
Large and consistent buybacks shrink the share count
watch: Net new client assets in wealth management and adviser headcount.
